Network & DNS settings

The resolver list behind the DNS & LB Lookup tool, and the registry of IPAM/DDI backends (EfficientIP, phpIPAM, NetBox) that SATOM uses to reserve addresses and publish DNS records.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSettings → Network & DNS → DNS Lookup / DNS Records (URL /settings/#tab-dnstool, /settings/#tab-dnsrecords)

What is it?#

The Network & DNS group has two tabs:

  • DNS Lookup — the DNS servers that the DNS & LB Lookup tool queries. Every enabled server becomes one column in the lookup results; all ADOMs share the list.
  • DNS Records — the registry of IPAM / DDI backends: the systems SATOM may use to hand out addresses (IPAM role) and publish names (DNS role). More than one backend is supported, each with its own roles, scope, priority and credential. Provisioning, the Server Policy wizard and ACME dns-01 challenges use it.

What does it do?#

  • DNS Lookup: stores a list of name + server rows, each individually enabled.
  • DNS Records: add, edit, enable/disable, test and delete backends. When a request needs a backend it is chosen as follows:
  1. 1Roleonly backends carrying the IPAM or DNS role asked for
  2. 2Most specific scopesub.example.com beats example.com; an unscoped backend answers anything but ranks last
  3. 3Priorityequal scope: the lowest priority number wins
  4. 4Tieequal scope and equal priority is refused and both backends are named
  • Pools are matched exactly, never by network containment: {ip}/16 does not cover {ip}/22. Zones are compared case-insensitively.

Requirements#

  • users.manage.
  • For a backend: its API URL and a credential (EfficientIP password, phpIPAM API app token or NetBox API token).

Permissions#

🔑Permission

All routes (POST /settings/dns-tool, /settings/dns-records/*) require users.manage. Without it the Network & DNS group is hidden and calls return 403. Using the DNS & LB Lookup tool itself is covered in DNS tool.

How to use#

Maintain the resolver list#

  1. Open Settings → Network & DNS → DNS Lookup.
  2. Edit existing rows or fill one of the three empty rows (Name, Server (IP / hostname), Enabled). To remove a server, clear its row.
  3. Click Save DNS servers. The flash reads "DNS server list saved (N servers)." and the page returns to the DNS Lookup tab.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: saving the resolver list returns to the DNS Lookup tab; before, the page opened on the first tab of the console.

Need more than three new servers? Save, and three new empty rows appear.

Add an IPAM/DDI backend#

  1. Open Settings → Network & DNS → DNS Records.
  2. Under Add a backend, fill Name, choose Provider, set Priority and Enabled.
  3. Tick the Roles: IPAM — hands out addresses and/or DNS — publishes records. A role the provider can never perform is disabled (phpIPAM shows This provider has no record CRUD in any installation.).
  4. Optionally restrict the scope: DNS zones this backend serves and IPAM pools this backend serves, one per line. Empty = catch-all.
  5. Fill the provider fields and the secret; keep Verify the certificate on.
  6. Click Test these values (tests the form without saving), then Save backend — the table shows the new row with status untested until you click its Test button.

Manage existing backends#

  • Edit loads the row into the form (secret left blank = keep the stored one).
  • Test probes the saved row and records the result (OK / error) in the table.
  • Disable / Enable toggles the row without deleting it.
  • Delete asks Delete the backend "<name>"?.

Configuration#

DNS Lookup#

Field Description Required Example
Name Column title in the lookup results, max 64 characters. Rows with no name or no server are dropped. Yes Internal
Server (IP / hostname) Letters, digits, ., : and - only; max 128 characters. Yes 192.0.2.53
Enabled Unticked servers stay in the list but are not queried. New rows are ticked by default. No on

DNS Records — common fields#

Field Description Required Example
Name Unique; what run logs and audit lines call the backend (max 64 characters). Yes ddi-prod
Provider EfficientIP SOLIDserver, phpIPAM or NetBox. Yes NetBox
Priority Whole number, default 100; lowest wins a tie. No 50
Enabled (In service) Default on. No on
Roles At least one. phpIPAM cannot carry the DNS role. NetBox may carry it (whether netbox-dns is installed is checked at use time). Yes IPAM + DNS
DNS zones this backend serves One per line, stored lower-case. Empty = any zone. No example.com
IPAM pools this backend serves One per line, matched exactly (case preserved). Empty = any pool. No 198.51.100.0/24
Secret (labelled Password, API app token or API token) Encrypted at rest, never returned to the browser. Required when adding; blank on edit keeps it. There is no "clear" option — delete the row to retire a credential. Add —
Verify the certificate TLS verification, default on. No on

Provider-specific fields#

Provider Fields
EfficientIP SOLIDserver Base URL, Username, DNS server (smart/appliance name), Default DNS view (optional), Default zone (used when a caller names none), Default IPAM pool (subnet id or name)
phpIPAM Base URL, API app id, Default IPAM pool (subnet id or CIDR)
NetBox Base URL, Default zone (used when a caller names none), Default IPAM pool (prefix id or CIDR)

A default zone or pool must lie inside the declared scope (if a scope is declared); otherwise the save is refused.

Example#

🧪Example — Split IPAM and DNS

  • ipam-main: phpIPAM, role IPAM only, pools 42 and 198.51.100.0/24, priority 100.
  • ddi-dns: EfficientIP, role DNS only, zones example.com, priority 100.
  • ddi-lab: EfficientIP, role DNS only, zones lab.example.com, priority 100.

A record for www.lab.example.com goes to ddi-lab (more specific scope); www.example.com goes to ddi-dns; an address from pool 42 comes from ipam-main.

Result#

  • The resolver list is stored in app_settings (dnstool.servers); audit settings.dns_tool.
  • Backends are rows of their own; audit entries settings.dns_backend.save, .toggle, .delete, .test. The last test result and error are kept on the row and shown in the table and on the Server Policy wizard's selector.
  • Allocations and records remember which backend created them, so a rollback goes back to that backend.

Troubleshooting#

"Invalid DNS server address: '…'"#

Solution — enter an IP address or a plain hostname without scheme, port suffix or spaces.

"A backend with neither role can never answer anything. Give it the IPAM role, the DNS role, or both — or delete it."#

Solution — tick at least one role.

"phpIPAM has no DNS record CRUD in any installation, so it cannot carry the DNS role. …"#

Solution — keep phpIPAM for addresses and point the DNS role at EfficientIP or NetBox.

"A credential is required to add a backend." / "Enter the credential — there is no saved backend to take it from yet."#

Solution — type the secret when adding or when testing an unsaved backend.

"Another backend is already called '…'."#

Solution — choose a unique name.

"the default zone '…' is not one of the zones this backend is scoped to (…) — …"#

Solution — add the default zone to the scope, or clear the default. The same rule applies to the default pool.

"N provisioning run(s) still hold this backend as the handle for the address or record they created. …"#

Possible causes — unfinished provisioning runs reference the backend for rollback.

Solution — finish or abort those runs in Provisioning, then delete.

Lookup or provisioning says no backend matches#

Possible causes — no enabled backend carries the role (no backend), backends exist but none claims the zone or pool and none is a catch-all (no match), or two backends tie on scope and priority (ambiguous).

Solution — register a backend, widen a scope, or change one priority. A fleet with no DDI is supported: publishing a name then only warns.

Advanced#

Advanced Upgrade and storage notes
  • An older single-provider configuration (dnsrecords.* settings) is folded into one unscoped backend on first start; its default zone and pool are kept as defaults, not as a scope.
  • The Test button on a saved row also records the provider's live capabilities (for example whether NetBox has netbox-dns).
  • Backend secrets are encrypted with the node key; they are not routed through the Vault.
